native_result.query: How does incarceration affect the wealth of black individuals based on their income levels?
native_result.HypoA: The negative impact of incarceration on wealth for black individuals may be less for the high-income group than those at lower wealth ranges.
native_result.HypoB: Among Black NLSY79 respondents, incarceration is associated with a near-complete stall — and, for those who started with some wealth, a reversal — of wealth accumulation, with the setback scaling with initial socioeconomic position (1985 wealth terciles as income proxy). In the lowest tercile (1985 median wealth ≈ $0), ever-jailed respondents remain pinned at $0 median wealth through 1996, capturing only ~30% of the wealth growth of non-jailed peers ($6,077 vs $20,203 winsorized mean change). In the middle tercile their median wealth change by 1996 is negative (−$1,000 vs +$6,231 for non-jailed); in the highest tercile it is strongly negative (−$5,800 vs +$8,825), i.e., jailed respondents in the top tercile end 1996 with LESS wealth than they had in 1985. The jailed-vs-never-jailed wealth gap widens monotonically with initial wealth (≈$14K, $28K, $52K in winsorized mean 1985→1996 change; jailed×top-tercile OLS interaction −$35.2K, p=0.017). So the dollar and proportional wealth setback is largest for Black individuals who started mid-to-high wealth, while the poorest third are locked out of accumulation entirely (median wealth stuck at $0). Descriptive association, not causal: baseline wealth differences, an overlapping 1985–1994 treatment window, and a coarse composite wealth measure limit interpretation.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Inspected data (12,013×6, no missing; race categories white/black/'hipanic'). 2) Restricted to Black respondents (n=3,013). 3) Stratified by terciles of 1985 composite wealth (pre-treatment baseline, proxy for income level). 4) Computed wealth changes 1985→1990 and 1985→1996 by ever_jailed within each tercile; reported cell sizes, medians, and 1%/99% winsorized means. 5) 1996 treated as main post-treatment contrast; 1990 as intermediate point (window 1985–1994 may still be active). 6) OLS on winsorized change with jailed×tercile interaction and sex control. 7) Brief race context comparison (optional). Script: analysis_nls_incarceration.py.
